notes_blind_original: Claim list: the exhibit is given as 'Figure 6', but in the published paper the Experiment 3 AIC comparison is Fig. 8 (p. 1021). Provenance: the shipped E3_analysis.R (SHA matches pin) computes fixed-effects lm AICs for Bayes/UPCO/Competence via MuMIn::dredge, with a comment saying to switch to lmer with (1|lab)+(1|Subject) for the mixed models. Prior-only and proportion AICs are computed with lmer at lines 239-240. The report's Table 3 values for Bayes/UPCO/Competence (410.086/497.267/506.928) come from lmer models the reproducer added (E3_analysis_FD.R on https://osf.io/uyrq8/), following that comment. The report says this AIC table (supplementary Figure 12) 'was not included in the provided code'. So C3-C5 match only via a trivial reproducer addition. The paper is also internally inconsistent here: it says Fig. 8's AICs are fixed-effects estimates, yet the printed values coincide with the mixed-model numbers. C1 severity: I chose P2 rather than P1 because it is a baseline heuristic comparison and the ranking and conclusion are unchanged. P1 is arguable, since beating the heuristics is a stated Exp 3 hypothesis. My own hypothesis, not the report's: inside an R formula, t/(t+f) is nesting syntax, not a proportion (no I()). That could explain why the code's value differs from whatever produced 1722. The report's headline is that results 'reproduce almost perfectly'. Some scripts (E1, parts of E3 after the AIC section) needed minor fixes to run. Hence 'computationally reproducible' is an acceptable alternative.
